analysis.title: Weekly Market Directions: High rates, higher interest payments
key_insights: US interest payments as a share of government revenue reached an all-time high of close to 20%, and interest costs were a main driver of higher federal spending in the fiscal year ended 30 September.
Amundi expects the US fiscal backdrop plus high inflation to keep bond market volatility elevated, and argues for a flexible, diversified approach with a global focus.
US October CPI rose 0.4% MoM above expectations, and core rose 0.3%, beating forecasts for a third straight month. Amundi says this confirms its view that the Fed will raise rates in the near term.
The US 10-year yield again reached the 5% level last week, driven by fiscal concerns and expectations of further Fed hikes.
Global equities rose on positive US and Japan earnings and renewed AI optimism, despite an abrupt leadership change at a leading technology company. European equities reached new highs.
Gold fell as higher yields reduced the appeal of a non-yielding asset.
UK GDP grew 0.2% in September after a flat August, beating expectations for no growth. Q3 output grew 0.7%, in line with forecasts.
India October CPI rose to 6.09% YoY, a two-year high and above the RBI tolerance band, driven by food prices up nearly 9% YoY. Core rose to 4.7% from 4.5% and the RBI is likely to hike again.
earnings_insights: Positive corporate earnings in the US and Japan supported global equities in the week to 13 November 2026. No specific EPS figures are given.
